description:
pkix-ct/src/log_list.rs:38-41

```rust
/// Submission base URL of the log. RFC 6962 §3 / §4 paths
/// (`ct/v1/add-chain`, `ct/v1/get-proof-by-hash`, etc.) are
/// resolved relative to this URL.
pub url: String,
```

The field is typed as `String`. The doc says it's a URL but provides
no guarantee that:

- It parses as a URL (could be `""`, `"not a url"`, `"http://[::1"`).
- It ends in a trailing `/` (RFC 6962 §3 paths are resolved
  relative; the canonical join behavior depends on the trailing
  slash convention).
- It uses `https` (a `http://` log endpoint is a downgrade
  vulnerability if accepted by an online fetcher).

Today, all values come from `CtLogList::from_google_log_list_json`
which doesn't validate. A caller writing an online CT submission
adapter has to re-validate every `log.url` defensively.

Recommendation: keep the field public as `String` for `no_std`
compatibility (a `url::Url` newtype pulls in `url` dep, which is
std+alloc only and may not be welcome here). But add an accessor
`CtLog::submission_url() -> Result<&str, Error>` that lazily
validates structure (non-empty, parses-as-URL via a hand-rolled or
feature-gated check). Or document explicitly:

> No guarantee is made that this string is a syntactically valid
> URL. Callers feeding it to an HTTP client must validate the format
> themselves.

Priority P3; not a correctness bug, just a defensive-forcing concern.

Note: `pkix-ct` is `no_std`, so a typed URL is awkward. Hand-rolled
validation in a `#[cfg(feature = "url-validation")]` adapter is the
likely best compromise.
title: CtLog::url: String has no doc-stated URL invariant — caller must validate
